howTo.title: Open a business in a commercial space
howTo.steps: Contact Economic Development (603-589-3260) for site help, then check the Land Use Code and zoning with the Planning Department (603-589-3090). File a Building and Landuse Application with Building Safety (603-589-3080) for any fit-up work; commercial submittals can be emailed to permits@nashuanh.gov with one paper plan set delivered to City Hall.

howTo.title: Outdoor dining permit
howTo.steps: Dining in the public right-of-way uses the Request for Right-Of-Way Dining form; dining on private or commercial property uses the Outdoor Dining Permit packet, checklist, Jotform upload and site plan review. Meet Fire Marshal, Public Health and Building requirements, and submit a hazardous weather plan if using canopies. A fire fee applies. Email OutdoorDining@nashuanh.gov.

howTo.title: Apply for 79-E downtown tax relief on a building rehab
howTo.steps: Projects in the Downtown Nashua Community Revitalization Tax Relief District that spend at least 15 percent of pre-rehab assessed value or $75,000 (whichever is less) and fit the Downtown Master Plan can apply. Submit the signed application to the Office of the Mayor-Economic Development; staff send it to the Board of Aldermen, which holds a public hearing and decides within 45 days.

source.label: City of Nashua, Downtown Nashua Tax Relief Incentive

howTo.title: Apply for a Revolving Loan Fund loan
howTo.steps: Businesses in or moving to Nashua and nearby towns can borrow up to $250,000 (most loans $10,000 to $50,000) for working capital, equipment or owner-occupied real estate. Start with a free pre-application to check eligibility; the full application follows if the project qualifies. Call 603-589-3070 for the current rate.

source.label: City of Nashua, Greater Nashua Revolving Loan Fund

howTo.title: Claim ERZ tax credits
howTo.steps: Firms that make a threshold capital investment and create new jobs in one of the city's ERZ areas (Downtown/Simon Street, Westwood Industrial Park, Southwood/Trafalgar, Spit Brook Road, Northeastern Blvd, Amherst Street, Perimeter Road/Nashua Airport) can apply using the state ERZ-2 form. Credits apply against the Business Profits Tax and Business Enterprise Tax up to $200,000. Contact the Office of the Mayor-Economic Development.

source.label: City of Nashua, ERZ Tax Credits

howTo.title: Find commercial space
howTo.steps: The Economic Development Division will help locate space from small shared startup offices to large turnkey lots and can run a customized site search. Call 603-589-3260 or review the ten business districts.

source.label: City of Nashua, Find Available Property

notices.title: Opportunity Zone 2.0 designations approved for 25 NH census tracts
notices.detail: Governor Ayotte announced U.S. Treasury approval of 25 tracts across all 10 counties, effective January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2036. The article does not name Nashua tracts; maps are on the state website.

notices.title: Chamber hosts gubernatorial candidates at Nashua business forum
notices.detail: Gov. Kelly Ayotte and challenger Cinde Warmington outlined competing visions on taxes, affordability, housing, health care and child care at a Greater Nashua Chamber of Commerce forum.

notices.title: Nashua on the Move: Co.Starters bootcamp, Millyard redevelopment, parking pilot, Main Street lighting
notices.detail: The October 2026 Economic Development newsletter reports Co.Starters entrepreneurship bootcamps with NH SBDC expected February or March 2027 (contact HannumL@nashuanh.gov), BIDA's selection of Lansing Melbourne Group for Millyard redevelopment of the former police training facility and Pine Street lot, an overnight residential parking pilot under consideration, permanent downtown tree lighting starting later in October, LaRose Alley upgrades targeted for summer 2027, and a new business recruitment marketing campaign.
